newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Chamber signs deal with non-miner unions.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Chamber signs deal with non-miner unions.

text.p: South Africa's Chamber of Mines employer body on Thursday signed a three-year wage agreement with two technical and administrative union bodies which would cover gold and coal sectors.

The deal is the first three-year deal in the mining industry and incorprates and agreement that mines "shall be allowed to conduct normal operations on every day of the year, except public holidays", the Chamber said.

The two officials organisations represent about 18,000 employees from the Administrative, Technical and Electronic Association of South Africa (ATEASA) and the Officials' Association of South Africa (OASA).
The two associations represent some 15,100 officials on gold mines and some 2,700 members on coal mines.

"The gold agreement means employment costs for the officials' category on gold mines will be a fixed, measurable figure for the next three years, allowing the mines greater certainty in their medium- and long-term policy and planning objectives," the Chamber said.

But it added that implementation of wage increases would be suspended until sufficient progress had been made bilaterally between mines and the associations at mine or group level on the arrangements to be put in place to allow for normal operations on all days except public holidays.
The coal agreement provides for nine percent increases from June 1997. In 1998 and 1999 increases of 8.5 and nine percent will apply, depending on the mining house involved.
Increases at Ingwe Coal Corporation Ltd in 1998 and 1999 will be linked to the rate of inflation, the Chamber said.
